text:
Alex: anyone else seeing DNS SRV lookups from GPU inference pods fail intermittently on the edge spot nodes?
Priya: seeing same. service discovery looks fine in control plane but pods can't reach peer replicas for gRPC. :confused:
Alex: quick check: EndpointSlice exists in ns inference for svc: inference-worker
Alex: ```
kubectl -n inference get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=inference-worker
NAME                          ADDRESS-TYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
inference-worker-5d8f9        IPv4           8080    10.50.3.12,10.50.7.8
```
Dylan: but on the node where pods fail ipvs has no backends
Dylan: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln
IP Virtual Server version: 1.2.1
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
# (no entries for 10.50.3.12 or svc cluster IP)
```
Matt: kube-proxy logs on that node show partial sync errors
Matt: ```
W0402 21:13:47.123456   1234 proxier.go:1427] failed to translate service "inference-worker": endpoints not ready
E0402 21:13:47.123458   1234 event.go:22] "EndpointSlice watch add failed" err="resourceVersion too old"
```
Sarah: these nodes are spot-edge pool with taint `spot=true:PreferNoSchedule` and custom egress NAT to local gateway. NAT gateway logs show TCP resets for kube-proxy health checks around the same time.
Alex: I suspect a race: EndpointSlice added quickly but kube-proxy on spot nodes is behind due to transient connectivity to kube-apiserver during kubelet pressure/ephemeral CPU starvation from batch provisioning (GPU init).
Priya: repro steps I used:
Priya: 1) scale inference-worker from 3->20 (adds pods to spot pool)
Priya: 2) watch EndpointSlice created
Priya: 3) some new pods get stuck with connection errors to peers
Priya: 4) `systemctl restart kube-proxy` on node -> services back immediately
Dylan: restart kube-proxy seems to force re-sync and pulls in endpoints
Matt: so it's a local agent state issue rather than control plane missing data
Alex: can we get kube-proxy metrics? specifically `kube_proxy_syncs_total` and last sync latency on those nodes
Sarah: metrics show a backlog spike and syncer timeouts at the same time as GPU init i/o
Alex: options:
- bump kube-proxy resync frequency on spot pool
- switch spot pool nodes to iptables mode instead of ipvs (less stateful)
- add a brief pre-init pause so kube-proxy can warm up before pods start accepting traffic
Priya: I'm leaning to adding a tiny init container that waits for service backends to appear before app starts (quick mitigation)
Matt: long-term we should avoid relying on kube-proxy ipvs statefulness on very ephemeral nodes, or make apiserver connectivity during init more robust (keepalive/proxy retries)
Dylan: can we schedule a canary: update daemonset to set --conntrack-max-per-core higher and increase `--sync-period` frequency from 30s -> 10s just for spot pool? small rollout to 1 node first
Alex: agree canary that change on spot pool only
Sarah: created a quick ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2987 (notes + logs)
Alex: action items:
- Priya: add init-check in inference-worker image (short wait + kubectl get endpointslice loop) -- PR by EOD
- Dylan: prepare kube-proxy canary manifest with adjusted flags, roll to 1 node tomorrow
- Matt: collect more kube-proxy logs/metrics for nodes that show the issue and attach to INF-2987
- infra-bot: please post a reminder in #eng-oncall when canary starts :eyes:
infra-bot: reminder scheduled: kube-proxy spot-pool canary will start 2025-04-03T15:00:00Z
Priya: thanks, will start on the init container and link PR
Alex: thanks team :thumbsup:
